name: Luckau
summary: After Bautzen Napoleon sent Oudinot's XII Corps north towards Berlin against Bülow, who had been gathering troops to cover the capital. Bülow, moving from Cottbus to rejoin his men at Jüterbog, stopped in the walled town of Luckau, and on the morning of 4 June Oudinot's leading division attacked it. Pacthod's battalions drove the allies back inside the walls but could not break in, and in the afternoon Bülow's reinforced cavalry fell on their flanks; Oudinot fell back south-west towards Dresden. The same day the armistice of Pläswitz was signed.

forces.name: Pacthod's Division
forces.summary: Oudinot's leading division, the only one he brought into action. It reached Luckau at nine in the morning, drove Bülow's outposts back into the walled town, and spent the day trying to break in, until Bülow's cavalry fell on its flanks and Oudinot drew off.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Wikipedia's account of Luckau, from Smith's Napoleonic Wars Data Book, which names the battalions engaged.
Its battalions were mostly young conscripts of the classes of 1813 and 1814. They are rated as ordinary Line, as they fought: the list's Wavering or Morale 5 would suit those who broke more readily.
The 1st Léger's one battalion is with the 7th Line as one regiment, shown as Line; the Neapolitan light battalions are shown as French Light. The batteries are as at Bautzen a fortnight before.
The division's two foot batteries, where the list allows one, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Oudinot's Cavalry
forces.summary: Two squadrons each of Bavarian and Hessian chevau-légers with Pacthod's attack, which were swept from the field when Bülow's cavalry came round the French flanks.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Westphalian 1812 list, as Beaumont's brigade is at Bautzen and Dennewitz; the Bavarian and Hessian chevau-légers are its Hussars.
After Wikipedia's account of Luckau, from Smith's Napoleonic Wars Data Book, which names the battalions engaged.
Beaumont commanded Oudinot's corps cavalry; Wikipedia doesn't say he was there, so his leading the force is ours.
Cavalry with no infantry brigade to allow it shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Bülow's Corps
forces.formation: Prussian III Corps, with Harpe's Russians
forces.summary: Bülow's Prussians, marching to rejoin his troops at Jüterbog, held the walled town of Luckau against Oudinot through the day; in the afternoon his cavalry, reinforced, struck the French flanks and Oudinot fell back, the day the armistice was agreed.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1813: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the 1813 brigade, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.

After Nafziger's return of the Prussian army for 1 April 1813 (813DCA), the nearest that gives Bülow's brigades; Wikipedia gives his force at Luckau as 16½ battalions, ten squadrons, a Cossack regiment and 58 guns, 15,800 men.

In the spring of 1813 the brigades had no Landwehr yet: each was two line regiments, with grenadier, reserve and Jäger battalions besides, so most have more line regiments, or more battalions in a regiment, than the list's brigade takes, which shows as historical departures.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.
Three line regiments, the 3rd East Prussian's three musketeer battalions, no Landwehr, and Oppen's cavalry brigade with one infantry brigade to allow it show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.
